title: Closing stream drainage cannot keep one low store and a runoff loss without a water-budget change
abstract: We test a restricted groundwater-disconnection model. With equal recharge and other outlets, reducing stream drainage capacity cannot lower a single store from the same initial state. After drought, cumulative runoff loss cannot exceed the initial storage deficit while storage stays below reference and the other outlet is nondecreasing with storage. We extend the test to an unknown store through an explicit capacity bound. Two exact synthetic models give the same one-metre shallow head shortfall and 25% less flow for 12 years. One exports 480 mm; the other stores 480 mm at depth. Shallow heads alone cannot separate them. A numerical solution checks the analytic recovery curve, and bounded-input tests check the storage bound. These are model results, not field estimates. The test needs a physical reference, representative head-to-volume conversion, and bounds on recharge and unobserved storage. It does not reject stream disconnection in Victoria. Code, proofs, synthetic results, source hashes and repeat instructions are included.

display.caption: Synthetic closure-only recovery and identical low-head records from export or hidden storage. All parameters are stated assumptions.
